eyebrow: TCM Wellness Reading · 中醫養生英文閱讀
lead_en: English reading passages that teach the principles of Chinese medicine — with vocabulary, comprehension questions, and a quick quiz in every lesson.
lead_zh: 用英文閱讀讀懂中醫的道理：每一課都有生字、閱讀理解與小測驗。

intro.en: This series is built the same way as our other reading lessons: an English passage first, vocabulary pulled straight out of that passage, and a Chinese translation available with one tap if you need it.
intro.zh: 這個系列跟站上其他閱讀教材做法一樣：先讀英文文章，生字直接從文章裡挑出來，需要的話點一下就能看中文翻譯。

intro.en: The topics are organized into units — Qi, Yin-Yang, the Five Elements, and more — and each unit keeps growing with new lessons over time. One lesson, one idea, explained clearly rather than a long list of tips.
intro.zh: 主題分成幾個大單元——氣、陰陽、五行……之後會持續加課。一課只講一個概念，不塞一堆要點。

intro.en: A short note before you start: these lessons explain ideas, not treatments. They don't diagnose, prescribe, or recommend acupuncture points. If something here feels personal, that's a reason to see a licensed doctor of Chinese medicine.
intro.zh: 開始前提醒一句：這裡講的是理論，不是治療。不辨證、不開方、不談針灸取穴。如果讀到某段特別有共鳴，請掛號給合格中醫師。

units.blurb_en: The idea everything else in Chinese medicine is built on.
units.blurb_zh: 後面的陰陽、臟腑、經絡全建立在這個概念上。

lessons.title: Qi Is Not "Energy"
lessons.blurb_en: The single biggest translation mistake in Chinese medicine — and why it matters.
lessons.blurb_zh: 中醫裡最常見的一個翻譯錯誤，也是最該先弄懂的一件事。
paras: When people first encounter Chinese medicine, they almost always meet the word qi in translation as "energy." This translation feels natural, but it causes more confusion than it solves. Energy, in the scientific sense, is something you can measure, store, and convert from one form into another. Qi is not that kind of thing. It is not a substance sitting somewhere, waiting to be used — it is closer to the body doing its work. When someone's qi is described as weak, the point is not that a battery has run low. The point is that the body's basic functions are not being carried out with full force.

This is one reason many teachers of Chinese medicine now leave the word qi untranslated, the same way English speakers keep words like karma and nirvana rather than force them into an English equivalent. Once qi becomes "energy," the next question is almost always the same: can this be measured with a machine? That question has already gone wrong, because it assumes qi is a quantity in the first place. Asking how much qi someone has is a bit like asking how much fitness a person has. Fitness is real — you can see its effects in how someone moves, breathes, and recovers from illness — but it is not a substance sitting inside the body, waiting to be weighed.

So the very first lesson in Chinese medicine has nothing to do with herbs or acupuncture. It is simply this: qi describes a pattern of function, not a form of energy. Get this distinction right, and every idea that follows — from the five functions of qi to the causes of fatigue — will rest on solid ground.
paras_zh: 第一次接觸中醫的人，幾乎都會先遇到「氣」被翻譯成 energy。這個翻譯聽起來很自然，卻製造了比它解決的還多的誤解。科學意義上的 energy 是可以被測量、儲存、轉換形式的東西；氣不是那種東西。氣不是放在某處等著被使用的物質，而更接近「身體正在運作」這件事本身。說某人氣虛，意思不是電池沒電了，而是身體的基本功能沒有被全力執行。

這是為什麼許多中醫老師現在傾向保留 qi 這個字不翻譯——就像英文使用者保留 karma、nirvana 這些字，而不硬找一個英文對應詞。一旦氣被譯成 energy，下一個問題幾乎必然出現：這可以用儀器測量嗎？這個問題從一開始就走錯了方向，因為它預設了氣是一種數量。問一個人有多少氣，有點像問一個人有多少 fitness。fitness 是真實的——你可以從一個人的動作、呼吸、病後恢復力看出它的效果——但它不是身體裡等著被秤重的一種物質。
所以中醫的第一課，跟藥草或針灸都沒有關係。它只是這件事：氣描述的是一種功能的模式，不是一種能量的形式。把這個分野弄對，後面所有的道理——從氣的五個功能，到疲勞的成因——才站得住腳。
questions: According to the passage, what is the difference between "energy" in the scientific sense and qi?
Why do many teachers of Chinese medicine prefer to leave the word qi untranslated?
What does the comparison between qi and "fitness" help explain?
answers: Energy can be measured, stored, and converted between forms, while qi describes the body's functions being carried out — it isn't a substance that exists on its own.
Because translating qi as "energy" invites the wrong kind of question, such as whether it can be measured with a machine, when qi was never meant to describe a measurable quantity.
It shows that something can be real and observable in its effects without being a physical substance that can be stored or weighed.

vocab.ex: Ice is a solid substance, while steam is a gas.
vocab.exzh: 冰是固態的物質，而蒸氣是氣態的。

vocab.ex: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity.
vocab.exzh: 太陽能板把陽光轉換成電力。

vocab.ex: The chef left the dish's French name untranslated on the menu.
vocab.exzh: 主廚把這道菜的法文名稱保留在菜單上，沒有翻譯。

vocab.ex: There isn't always an English equivalent for a Chinese idiom.
vocab.exzh: 中文成語不一定有對等的英文說法。

vocab.ex: Don't assume the store is open just because the lights are on.
vocab.exzh: 不要因為燈亮著就認定店有開。

vocab.ex: Understanding the distinction between "hear" and "listen" changed how she taught.
vocab.exzh: 理解「聽到」和「聆聽」的區別，改變了她教學的方式。

vocab.ex: He felt a wave of fatigue after the long flight.
vocab.exzh: 長途飛行後，他感到一陣疲勞襲來。

quiz.q: What is the main difference between "energy" (in the scientific sense) and qi, according to the passage?
options: Energy is more powerful than qi.
Energy can be measured and converted; qi describes the body's functions being carried out.
Qi can be stored in the body while energy cannot.
There is no real difference — they mean exactly the same thing.

quiz.q: Why do many teachers of Chinese medicine now leave the word qi untranslated?
options: Because there is no English alphabet that can spell it correctly.
Because English speakers cannot pronounce Chinese words.
Because translating it as "energy" leads to the wrong kind of question, like whether it can be measured with a machine.
Because qi is a trademarked term in Chinese medicine.

quiz.q: What does comparing qi to "fitness" help explain?
options: That qi, like fitness, can be purchased at a gym.
That something can be real and observable in its effects without being a physical substance.
That qi is a form of physical exercise.
That fitness and qi are unrelated concepts.

lessons.boundary_en: This lesson explains an idea, not a treatment. If something here feels personal, see a licensed doctor of Chinese medicine rather than self-diagnosing.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這是理論介紹，不是治療建議；如果讀到某段特別有共鳴，請掛號給合格中醫師，而不是自行對照症狀判斷。

lessons.title: The Five Jobs of Qi
lessons.blurb_en: Why weak qi makes a person tired, cold, and prone to catching colds — traced back to one principle, not a list to memorize.
lessons.blurb_zh: 氣虛的人為什麼會累、會冷、常常感冒？從一個原理往下推，不用背清單。
paras: Chinese medicine describes qi as doing five jobs in the body. It moves things along — pushing blood through the vessels, fluids through their channels, and the organs through their daily work. It keeps the body warm, which is why healthy hands and feet stay comfortably warm rather than cold. It defends the body against outside threats, which is why some people catch a cold at the first change of season while others seem to shrug it off. It holds things in their place, keeping blood inside the vessels and sweat from leaking out for no reason. And it transforms what a person eats and drinks into something the body can actually use.

These five jobs are not five separate topics to memorize. They are five expressions of the same underlying activity. Once you understand them as one thing seen from five angles, the symptoms of weak qi stop looking like a random list and start looking like a single pattern, read backward. If qi cannot move things along, a person feels tired and doesn't want to talk. If it cannot keep the body warm, the hands and feet turn cold. If it cannot defend the body, colds become frequent. If it cannot hold things in place, a person may sweat without any exertion at all. If it cannot transform food into something usable, appetite drops even though the person is eating normally.

This is the real difference between understanding a principle and memorizing a checklist. A checklist of five symptoms is easy to forget. A principle that explains why those five symptoms show up together — and predicts a sixth one you haven't seen yet — is much harder to lose.
paras_zh: 中醫講氣在身體裡做五件事：推動——把血液推過血管、把水液推過通道、把臟腑推動去做每天的工作；溫煦——維持體溫，這是為什麼健康的手腳是舒服地溫暖，而不是冰冷；防禦——抵擋外來的威脅，這是為什麼有人一換季就感冒，有人卻好像完全不受影響；固攝——把東西固定在該在的位置，讓血液留在血管裡、汗不會無緣無故流出來；還有氣化——把吃進去、喝進去的東西轉變成身體真正能用的東西。
這五件事不是五個要分別背下來的主題，而是同一個底層活動從五個角度看出來的樣子。一旦你把它們理解成一件事，氣虛的症狀就不再像是一份隨機的清單，而是同一個模式倒過來讀。推不動，人就會累、不想講話；溫不了，手腳就會冰冷；防不住，就常常感冒；固不住，可能無緣無故就流汗；化不了，就算正常吃飯，食慾也會下降。
這正是「理解一個原理」跟「背一份檢查清單」的真正差別。五個症狀的清單很容易忘記；一個能解釋這五個症狀為什麼會一起出現——還能預測你還沒看過的第六個症狀——的原理，卻很難丟掉。
questions: List the five jobs of qi described in the passage.
Why does the passage say these five jobs are "not five separate topics to memorize"?
According to the passage, what happens to a person's appetite when qi cannot transform food properly, and why?
answers: Moving things along, keeping the body warm, defending against outside threats, holding things in place, and transforming food and drink into something usable.
Because they are five expressions of one underlying activity — once qi is weak, all five show up as one connected pattern, not five random, unrelated problems.
Appetite drops, even though the person may be eating a normal amount, because the body isn't turning food into something it can actually use.

vocab.ex: A strong immune system helps defend the body against infection.
vocab.exzh: 強健的免疫系統有助於保護身體對抗感染。

vocab.ex: She was out of breath after only mild exertion.
vocab.exzh: 她只是稍微用力就喘不過氣。

vocab.ex: Cooking transforms raw ingredients into a finished dish.
vocab.exzh: 烹飪把生的食材轉變成一道完成的菜。

vocab.ex: His appetite disappeared after he caught the flu.
vocab.exzh: 他得了流感之後，食慾就消失了。

vocab.ex: Frequent hand-washing helps prevent colds.
vocab.exzh: 頻繁洗手有助於預防感冒。

vocab.ex: The doctor noticed a pattern in when the headaches occurred.
vocab.exzh: 醫師注意到頭痛發生的時間有一個模式。

vocab.ex: The pilot went through the checklist before takeoff.
vocab.exzh: 飛行員在起飛前檢查了整份清單。

quiz.q: According to the passage, what happens when qi cannot "hold things in place"?
options: A person feels cold all the time.
A person may sweat without any exertion at all.
A person catches colds more easily.
A person's appetite increases.

quiz.q: Why does the passage compare the five jobs of qi to "one thing seen from five angles" rather than five separate topics?
options: Because only one of the five jobs is actually true.
Because they are five expressions of the same underlying activity, so weak qi shows up as one connected pattern.
Because Chinese medicine only recognizes one function of qi.
Because the five jobs happen in a strict order, one after another.

quiz.q: What is the "real difference" the passage describes between understanding a principle and memorizing a checklist?
options: A checklist is always more accurate than a principle.
A principle only applies to healthy people, not sick ones.
A principle explains why symptoms occur together and can predict new ones, while a checklist is easy to forget.
There is no real difference between the two.

lessons.boundary_en: This lesson explains an idea, not a treatment. A symptom like "frequent colds" can have many causes — a doctor of Chinese medicine, not this reading, should judge which one applies to you.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這是理論介紹，不是治療建議；同一個「容易感冒」可能有很多原因，該由中醫師判斷，不是這篇文章。

lessons.title: When Overexertion Drains Qi
lessons.blurb_en: Four ancient characters explain the most common cause of weak qi — and "overexertion" means more than physical tiredness.
lessons.blurb_zh: 《黃帝內經》四個字講完氣虛最常見的成因，而「勞」不只是體力上的累。
paras: The Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic, one of the oldest texts in Chinese medicine, states the idea in four characters: overexertion drains qi. The same chapter goes even further, claiming that a hundred diseases arise from qi. What makes this idea useful today is what counts as "overexertion." It is not limited to physical labor. Thinking too much, carrying responsibility for too long, and never quite letting go of a worry are all treated as forms of overexertion in Chinese medicine — the same category as working a double shift.

Qi behaves like any resource that gets spent. If it is drawn on constantly and never replenished, the result is depletion. And the classic signs of depleted qi line up closely with the five functions from the last lesson: a person feels tired and doesn't want to talk, catches colds easily, and may sweat with the smallest amount of exertion.
None of this is a diagnosis. It is a description of a mechanism — spending without replenishing — that anyone can recognize in their own life, long before it becomes a medical problem.
paras_zh: 《黃帝內經》——中醫最古老的典籍之一——用四個字講完了這個概念：勞則氣耗。同一篇甚至講得更重：百病生於氣。這個概念到今天還有用的地方，在於什麼算是「勞」。它不只限於體力勞動。思慮過度、長期承擔責任、放不下一個擔心，在中醫裡都被當成「勞」的一種——跟連上兩班一樣算在同一個範疇裡。
氣的行為就像任何會被花掉的資源。如果持續被支出、卻從來沒有回補，結果就是耗竭。而氣耗竭的典型徵象，剛好對上上一課的五個功能：人會累、不想講話、容易感冒，稍微用一點力就可能流汗。
這些都不是診斷，而是一種機制的描述——支出而不回補——任何人都能在自己的生活裡認出來，早在它變成醫療問題之前。
questions: What does the phrase "overexertion drains qi" mean, according to the passage?
According to the passage, why does worrying for a long time count as a kind of "overexertion," even without physical labor?
How do the symptoms described in this passage connect to the five functions of qi from the previous lesson?
answers: It means that qi is used up when a person is overexerted — whether the exertion is physical, mental, or emotional.
Because Chinese medicine treats sustained worry and responsibility as a drain on the same resource — qi — that physical labor draws on.

The symptoms — tiredness, frequent colds, and sweating with little exertion — are what happens when qi's five functions (moving, warming, defending, holding, transforming) are no longer being carried out with full force.

vocab.ex: Long meetings drain his energy by the end of the day.
vocab.exzh: 冗長的會議到了一天結束時會耗盡他的精力。

vocab.ex: Depletion of iron in the body can lead to fatigue.
vocab.exzh: 體內鐵質的耗竭會導致疲勞。

vocab.ex: Drink water regularly to replenish what you lose through sweat.
vocab.exzh: 定期喝水以補充流汗流失的水分。

vocab.ex: Time is a limited resource, just like money.
vocab.exzh: 時間跟金錢一樣，是有限的資源。

vocab.ex: Sustained effort over months matters more than one hard day.
vocab.exzh: 持續好幾個月的努力，比一天拚命更重要。

vocab.ex: Understanding the mechanism behind a habit makes it easier to change.
vocab.exzh: 理解一個習慣背後的機制，會讓它更容易被改變。

quiz.q: According to the passage, which of these counts as "overexertion" in Chinese medicine?
options: Only heavy physical labor.
Only a lack of sleep.
Thinking too much and carrying responsibility for too long, as well as physical labor.
Eating too much food.

quiz.q: What does the passage mean by saying qi "behaves like any resource that gets spent"?
options: Qi can be bought and sold like money.
If qi is drawn on constantly without being replenished, the result is depletion.
Qi disappears completely after a single use.
Only wealthy people have enough qi.

quiz.q: What is the relationship between the symptoms in this lesson and the five functions of qi from the previous lesson?
options: They are unrelated ideas from two different medical systems.
The symptoms described here are what happens when qi's five functions are no longer carried out with full force.
The five functions only apply to elderly patients.
The symptoms only occur if a person ignores all five functions equally.

lessons.boundary_en: This lesson explains a mechanism, not a diagnosis. If tiredness, frequent colds, and unexplained sweating show up together, that's worth a visit to a licensed doctor of Chinese medicine.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這是機制的描述，不是診斷；如果疲倦、容易感冒、無故流汗同時出現，值得掛號給合格中醫師看看。

lessons.title: Restoring Qi Without Medicine
lessons.blurb_en: The basic principle for restoring qi has nothing to do with herbs — the hard part is following through.
lessons.blurb_zh: 補氣的大原則其實很簡單，而且不需要吃藥——難的是做到。
paras: If overexertion drains qi, then restoring it should, in theory, be simple: spend less, and replenish more. Chinese medicine turns this into four practical habits. Reduce the mental load of constant worry and responsibility. Go to sleep earlier, ideally before eleven at night, when the body's yang qi is naturally being nourished. Eat and drink with some restraint, rather than relying on cold or raw food. And avoid sweating to excess, since heavy sweating draws directly on qi.

These four habits are not four unrelated tips picked at random. Each one addresses a different one of the five functions from earlier in this course. Reducing mental load cuts down on what qi has to move. Sleeping earlier increases how much qi gets replenished overnight. Eating with restraint keeps the transforming function from being overworked. Avoiding excessive sweating protects the holding function from being forced to work overtime.

In other words, the four habits are the same five-function framework, simply read in reverse: instead of asking what happens when qi runs low, they ask what protects it from running low in the first place. None of them require a prescription. All of them require follow-through, which is precisely why they are harder than they sound.
paras_zh: 如果勞則氣耗，理論上要補氣就該很簡單：少支出，多回補。中醫把它變成四個具體的生活習慣：減少思慮與責任帶來的心理負荷；早點睡，理想上在晚上十一點以前，這時身體的陽氣正在被滋養；飲食有所節制，不要靠冰的或生冷的食物；避免過度流汗，因為大量流汗會直接耗損氣。
這四個習慣不是四個隨機挑出來、彼此無關的小撇步。每一個都對應著這門課前面提過的五功能裡的不同一項。減少心理負荷，減少了氣需要去推動的量；早睡，增加了夜間氣被回補的量；飲食節制，避免了氣化功能被過度使用；避免過度流汗，保護了固攝功能不被迫超時工作。
換句話說，這四個習慣就是同一套五功能框架，只是反過來讀：不是問氣不足時會發生什麼，而是問要怎麼保護氣，不讓它一開始就不足。這些都不需要藥方；需要的是持之以恆——這正是為什麼它們聽起來簡單，做起來卻困難。
questions: List the four habits for restoring qi described in the passage.
How does the passage connect these four habits to the five functions of qi taught earlier in the course?
According to the last paragraph, why are these habits harder than they sound?
answers: Reducing mental load, sleeping earlier, eating and drinking with restraint, and avoiding excessive sweating.

Each habit protects a specific function — reducing mental load lightens what qi must move, earlier sleep increases replenishment, restrained eating protects the transforming function, and avoiding excess sweat protects the holding function.
Because none of them require a prescription — they only require consistent follow-through, which is harder to sustain than following a one-time instruction.

vocab.ex: He showed real restraint by not finishing the whole cake.
vocab.exzh: 他展現了真正的節制，沒有把整個蛋糕吃完。

vocab.ex: A balanced diet nourishes both the body and the mind.
vocab.exzh: 均衡的飲食滋養身體，也滋養心靈。

vocab.ex: Excessive screen time before bed can disrupt sleep.
vocab.exzh: 睡前過度使用螢幕會擾亂睡眠。

vocab.ex: The teacher gave students a framework for organizing their essays.
vocab.exzh: 老師給了學生一個組織文章的框架。

vocab.ex: Good ideas mean nothing without follow-through.
vocab.exzh: 好點子如果沒有貫徹到底，就沒有意義。

vocab.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for antibiotics.
vocab.exzh: 醫師開了一張抗生素的處方。

quiz.q: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT one of the four habits for restoring qi?
options: Sleeping earlier, ideally before eleven at night.
Eating and drinking with some restraint.
Taking an herbal supplement every morning.
Avoiding sweating to excess.

quiz.q: How does the passage connect "eating with restraint" to the five functions of qi?
options: It keeps the transforming function from being overworked.
It has no connection to any of the five functions.
It only affects the defending function.
It replaces the need for sleep.

quiz.q: Why does the passage say these four habits are "harder than they sound"?
options: Because they require expensive ingredients.
Because they require a doctor's prescription.
Because they require consistent follow-through rather than a one-time action.
Because they must be done in a specific numerical order.

lessons.boundary_en: These are general lifestyle principles, not a prescription. If you already have clear symptoms, see a licensed doctor of Chinese medicine for a proper diagnosis rather than guessing at a fix.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這裡講的是生活原則，不是處方；已經有明顯症狀的話，請找合格中醫師辨證，不要自己猜方向。

lessons.title: Explaining Qi to a Friend
lessons.blurb_en: A model explanation for when a friend asks, "What is qi?" — built from everything covered in this unit.
lessons.blurb_zh: 當朋友問「氣是什麼？」，一段可以直接照講的示範回答，整合這個單元學過的一切。
paras: Suppose a friend who has never studied Chinese medicine asks, "What is qi?" A good answer follows a specific order, because getting the order right is what keeps the conversation from going in the wrong direction. Start here: "Qi isn't a substance you store — it's closer to the body doing its work. When we say someone's qi is weak, we're not saying a battery ran low; we're saying the body's functions aren't being carried out with full force."

Next, explain what those functions are: "In Chinese medicine, qi does five things: it moves things along, keeps you warm, defends you, holds things in place, and turns what you eat into something your body can use." Only after this should the conversation turn to measurement, because that question will come up regardless: "It's not a measurable quantity in the physics sense — it's a way of describing patterns of function. Asking how much qi there is is a bit like asking how much fitness someone has: real, observable in its effects, but not a substance sitting somewhere."

Finally, close with the boundary that matters most: "None of this replaces seeing a doctor. Qi is a framework for understanding how the body works as a whole — not a diagnosis, and not a substitute for one." Explaining qi well is not about finding a clever English word to replace it. It's about walking someone through the idea in an order that keeps them from getting stuck on the wrong question too early.
paras_zh: 假設一位從沒學過中醫的朋友問：「氣是什麼？」一個好的回答要按照特定的順序來講，因為順序對了，對話才不會走偏。可以這樣開始：「氣不是一種你儲存起來的物質，它更接近身體正在運作這件事本身。當我們說一個人氣虛，不是在說電池沒電了，而是在說身體的功能沒有被全力執行。」
接著，解釋這些功能是什麼：「在中醫裡，氣做五件事：它推動事物、讓你保持溫暖、保護你、把東西固定住、把你吃的東西變成身體能用的東西。」只有講完這些之後，才輪到談測量，因為這個問題遲早會被問到：「從物理學的意義上，它不是一個可以測量的量——它是一種描述功能模式的方式。問氣有多少，有點像問一個人有多少 fitness：真實存在、能從它的效果看出來，但不是放在某處等著被秤重的一種物質。」
最後，用最重要的那條邊界收尾：「這一切都不能取代看醫生。氣是理解身體如何整體運作的一個框架——不是診斷，也不能替代診斷。」把氣解釋好，重點不是找到一個聰明的英文字來取代它，而是用一個順序帶著對方走過這個概念，不讓他們太早卡在錯的問題上。
questions: According to the passage, why does the order of an explanation matter as much as its content?
What is the purpose of comparing qi to "fitness" in this kind of conversation?
Why does the passage suggest ending the explanation with a boundary about seeing a doctor?
answers: Because if the wrong question — such as one about measurement — comes up too early, the listener gets stuck thinking of qi as a measurable substance, which makes the rest of the explanation harder to follow.
It shows that something can be real and observable in its effects without being a physical substance that can be measured or stored, which helps the listener let go of the "energy" framework.
Because without that boundary, a listener might mistakenly think the explanation is offering medical advice, rather than a cultural and theoretical framework.

lessons.boundary_en: Explaining qi to a friend is a cultural and language exercise, not medical advice. If your friend has a real health concern, the answer is always to see a doctor — Chinese or Western.

units.blurb_en: Not good versus bad — a pair of complementary functions that only make sense together.
units.blurb_zh: 不是善惡二分，是一對只有合在一起才有意義的互補功能。

lessons.title: Yin and Yang Are Not "Good" and "Bad"
lessons.blurb_en: The most common misreading of yin-yang, corrected before it can cause any more confusion.
lessons.blurb_zh: 陰陽最常見的誤解，先在這裡糾正過來。
paras: After qi, the next idea a student of Chinese medicine meets is yin and yang — and the most common misunderstanding arrives almost immediately. In popular culture, yin often gets treated as "bad" or "dark" and yang as "good" or "light," the way a villain and a hero get cast in a story. Chinese medicine uses the words very differently. Yin and yang describe a pair of complementary functions, not a moral judgment. Yin is associated with substance, rest, cooling, and the body's interior; yang is associated with function, activity, warming, and the body's exterior. Neither one is better than the other, in the same way that inhaling is not "better" than exhaling.

The two also cannot exist without each other. A body with no yin — no substance, no fluids, no rest — would have nothing for yang to warm or move. A body with no yang — no function, no activity, no warmth — would have substance sitting perfectly still, doing nothing. Health, in this framework, is not about maximizing yang and minimizing yin, or the reverse. It is about the two staying in a working relationship with each other, each doing its job without overtaking the other.

This is why a Chinese medicine practitioner almost never says a patient has "too much yin" or "too little yang" as a final verdict. Those words only mean something in relation to each other, at a particular moment, for a particular person. Learning yin-yang is really learning to stop asking "which one is winning" and start asking "are they still working together."
paras_zh: 學完氣之後，中醫學生接下來會遇到的下一個概念是陰陽——而最常見的誤解幾乎馬上就會出現。在流行文化裡，陰常被當成「壞的」或「黑暗的」，陽被當成「好的」或「光明的」，就像故事裡的反派跟英雄。中醫用這兩個字的方式完全不同。陰陽描述的是一對互補的功能，不是道德判斷。陰跟物質、休息、寒涼、身體的內部有關；陽跟功能、活動、溫熱、身體的外部有關。兩者沒有誰比較好，就像吸氣不會比呼氣「更好」一樣。
這兩者也無法脫離對方單獨存在。一個完全沒有陰——沒有物質、沒有津液、沒有休息——的身體，會讓陽無物可溫、無物可推動。一個完全沒有陽——沒有功能、沒有活動、沒有溫熱——的身體，物質會完全靜止，什麼都做不了。在這個框架裡，健康不是把陽最大化、把陰最小化，或反過來。健康是讓兩者維持一種持續運作的關係，各自做好自己的工作，不壓過對方。
這就是為什麼中醫師幾乎不會把「陰太多」或「陽太少」當成一個最終定論來講。這些字只有在彼此相對、在特定時刻、對特定的人身上才有意義。學陰陽，其實是在學怎麼停止問「哪一個贏了」，開始問「他們還有沒有一起運作」。
questions: According to the passage, why is it a mistake to treat yin as simply "bad" and yang as simply "good"?
What does the passage mean by saying yin and yang "cannot exist without each other"?
According to the passage, what should the real question be, instead of asking "which one is winning"?
answers: Because in Chinese medicine, yin and yang describe complementary functions — substance/rest/cooling versus function/activity/warming — not a moral judgment of good versus bad.

It means that yin (substance, rest) gives yang (function, activity) something to act on, and yang gives yin the activity that keeps it from being static and useless — each needs the other to make sense.
Whether yin and yang are still working together in a balanced relationship, rather than which one currently has the upper hand.

quiz.q: According to the passage, what is the key mistake in treating yin as "bad" and yang as "good"?
options: There is no such thing as yin and yang in Chinese medicine.
Yin and yang are complementary functions, not a moral judgment of good versus bad.
Yang is always good and yin is always bad in Chinese medicine, too.
Chinese medicine agrees with the popular culture description.

quiz.q: Why can't a body have "no yin" and still have healthy yang, according to the passage?
options: Because yang needs substance and rest (yin) to have something to act on.
Because yin produces yang directly, like a factory.
Because yang and yin are actually the same thing.
Because a body without yin would have too much yang.

quiz.q: According to the passage, what is the real question to ask about a person's yin-yang, instead of "which one is winning"?
options: Which one is more expensive to treat.
Which one the patient prefers.
Whether yin and yang are still working together in balance.
Which one was diagnosed first.

lessons.boundary_en: This lesson explains a concept, not a diagnosis. "Balance" here is a framework for thinking, not a specific health metric — a licensed doctor of Chinese medicine is who can assess an individual case.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這是概念說明，不是診斷；「平衡」在這裡是一種思考框架，不是一個具體的健康指標，個案評估請找合格中醫師。

lessons.title: How Qi Deficiency Splits Into Yang and Yin
lessons.title_zh: 氣虛怎麼分成陽虛與陰虛
lessons.blurb_en: Qi deficiency has a direction — and knowing which one changes what actually helps.
lessons.blurb_zh: 氣虛是有方向的——弄清楚哪個方向，才知道什麼真的有幫助。
paras: The first unit of this course ended with qi deficiency — a state where the body's basic functions are not being carried out with full force. Once yin and yang enter the picture, qi deficiency can be described more precisely, because it can lean in one of two directions. When the "warming" and "moving" side of qi runs low, the result is called yang deficiency: a person feels cold, especially in the hands and feet, moves slowly, and often prefers warm drinks and warm weather. When the "cooling" and "moistening" side runs low instead, the result is called yin deficiency: a person may feel warm in the afternoon or evening, have a dry mouth, and sleep restlessly despite feeling tired.

It helps to picture qi as a single team that yin and yang split between them. Yang qi handles warming and moving; yin qi handles moistening and calming. Plain qi deficiency is a general shortage of staff. Yang deficiency and yin deficiency describe which side of the team is short-staffed. A person can, in theory, have signs of both at once, which is simply qi deficiency that has not yet settled clearly into one direction.

None of this is something to self-diagnose from a reading passage. What matters here is the logic: Chinese medicine rarely stops at a single, flat label like "weak qi." It keeps asking a more specific question — weak in which direction — because the answer changes what actually helps.
paras_zh: 這門課的第一個單元最後停在氣虛——身體的基本功能沒有被全力執行的狀態。陰陽這個概念加進來之後，氣虛可以講得更精確，因為它可以偏向兩個方向的其中一個。當氣裡「溫煦」和「推動」的那一側不足，結果叫做陽虛：人會怕冷，尤其是手腳，動作變慢，通常偏好溫熱的飲料和天氣。當「滋潤」和「安定」的那一側不足，結果叫做陰虛：人可能在下午或傍晚覺得燥熱，口乾，雖然疲倦卻睡不安穩。
把氣想像成一支被陰陽兩邊分掉的隊伍會比較好理解。陽氣負責溫煦和推動；陰氣負責滋潤和安定。單純的氣虛是整體人手不足；陽虛跟陰虛講的是隊伍的哪一邊人手不足。理論上一個人可以同時有兩邊的跡象，那只是還沒明確偏向某一個方向的氣虛。
這些都不是要你從一篇閱讀文章裡自我診斷。這裡重要的是背後的邏輯：中醫很少停在一個籠統的標籤，像是「氣虛」，就結束。它會繼續問一個更具體的問題——虛在哪個方向——因為答案會改變真正有幫助的做法。
questions: According to the passage, what is the difference between yang deficiency and yin deficiency?
Why does the passage compare qi to "a single team that yin and yang split between them"?
According to the last paragraph, why does Chinese medicine avoid stopping at a flat label like "weak qi"?
answers: Yang deficiency is a shortage of the warming/moving side of qi (cold, slow, prefers warmth), while yin deficiency is a shortage of the cooling/moistening side (afternoon warmth, dry mouth, restless sleep despite tiredness).

Because it helps explain that yang qi and yin qi handle different jobs within the same overall resource — general qi deficiency is a shortage of the whole team, while yang or yin deficiency describes which side is short-staffed.
Because asking "weak in which direction" gives a more specific answer, and that more specific answer is what actually changes what kind of help is appropriate.

quiz.q: According to the passage, what happens when the "warming and moving" side of qi runs low?
options: Yin deficiency, with symptoms like a dry mouth and restless sleep.
Yang deficiency, with symptoms like feeling cold and moving slowly.
The person becomes immune to illness.
Qi disappears completely.

quiz.q: What does yin qi handle, according to the "team" comparison in the passage?
options: Warming and moving.
Moistening and calming.
Digestion only.
Physical strength only.

quiz.q: Why does the passage say Chinese medicine keeps asking "weak in which direction" instead of stopping at "weak qi"?
options: Because a more specific answer changes what kind of help is appropriate.
Because "weak qi" is not a real concept.
Because doctors are required to ask multiple questions by law.
Because it makes the diagnosis take longer, which increases cost.

lessons.boundary_en: This lesson explains a distinction, not a self-test. Whether a set of symptoms points to yang deficiency, yin deficiency, or something else entirely is a judgment for a licensed doctor of Chinese medicine to make.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這是分類邏輯的說明，不是自我檢測；一組症狀究竟是陽虛、陰虛，還是別的情況，判斷交給合格中醫師。

lessons.title: The Four Relationships Between Yin and Yang
lessons.blurb_en: Opposition, interdependence, waxing-waning, and transformation — four angles on the same moving system.
lessons.blurb_zh: 對立制約、互根互用、消長平衡、相互轉化——同一個系統的四個角度。
paras: Chinese medicine describes yin and yang as connected through four different kinds of relationship, and each one answers a different question about how change happens in the body. The first is opposition: yin and yang restrain each other, the way cold restrains heat and heat restrains cold. If one grows unchecked, it naturally holds the other back. The second is interdependence: neither one can exist without the other, the way a shadow cannot exist without light. Yin provides the substance that yang acts on; yang provides the activity that keeps yin from becoming stagnant.

The third relationship is called waxing and waning: yin and yang do not stay fixed — they shift back and forth constantly, the way day gradually gives way to night and back again. A small increase in one is normally matched by a small decrease in the other, keeping the overall balance steady. The fourth relationship is transformation: under the right conditions, yin can convert into yang and yang can convert into yin, the way water can become steam and steam can become water again. This is the relationship that explains sudden change — a long illness marked by cold, quiet symptoms (yin) can, at a certain point, suddenly flip into a hot, agitated state (yang), and Chinese medicine treats this as a known pattern, not a mystery.

These four relationships are not four separate rules to memorize in isolation. They describe one continuously moving system, seen from four different angles: how the two hold each other in check, how they depend on each other, how they shift gradually, and how they can suddenly flip. Together, they explain why "balance" in Chinese medicine is never a fixed point — it is a moving target that a healthy body keeps hitting, over and over, without ever settling into one extreme.
paras_zh: 中醫講陰陽之間有四種不同的關係，每一種都回答身體裡「變化怎麼發生」的一個不同問題。第一種是對立制約：陰陽互相牽制，就像冷會抑制熱、熱也會抑制冷。如果其中一個不受限制地增長，另一個自然會把它拉回來。第二種是互根互用：兩者都無法脫離對方獨立存在，就像影子不能沒有光而存在。陰提供物質讓陽去作用；陽提供活動讓陰不至於停滯。

第三種關係叫做消長平衡：陰陽不是固定不變的——它們持續來回移動，就像白天逐漸讓位給黑夜，再逐漸回到白天。一方小幅增加，通常會對應另一方小幅減少，讓整體維持穩定。第四種關係是相互轉化：在適當的條件下，陰可以轉變成陽，陽也可以轉變成陰，就像水可以變成蒸氣，蒸氣也可以再變回水。這個關係解釋了突然的變化——一場以寒冷、安靜症狀（陰）為主的長期疾病，可能在某個時間點突然翻轉成燥熱、躁動的狀態（陽），中醫把這當成一個已知的模式，不是一個謎。
這四種關係不是四條要分開背誦的規則。它們描述的是同一個持續在動的系統，從四個不同的角度看：兩者怎麼互相牽制、怎麼互相依存、怎麼漸進地移動、又怎麼會突然翻轉。合起來，它們解釋了為什麼中醫講的「平衡」從來不是一個固定的點——它是一個健康的身體不斷重新命中的移動目標，不會停在某一個極端上。
questions: According to the passage, what is the difference between the "opposition" relationship and the "interdependence" relationship between yin and yang?
What everyday comparison does the passage use to explain the "waxing and waning" relationship?
According to the passage, how does the "transformation" relationship explain a sudden change in illness, such as a cold state suddenly becoming a hot one?
answers: Opposition means yin and yang restrain each other so neither grows unchecked, like cold and heat holding each other back, while interdependence means neither can exist without the other, like light and shadow.
The passage compares it to day gradually giving way to night and back again, with small shifts in one side matched by small shifts in the other.

It explains that under the right conditions, yin can convert into yang (and the reverse), the way water can become steam — so a long, cold, quiet illness can suddenly flip into a hot, agitated state, following a known pattern rather than being a mystery.

vocab.ex: A good leader restrains their temper even under pressure.
vocab.exzh: 好的領導者即使在壓力下也能抑制脾氣。

vocab.ex: The stagnant water in the pond had not moved for weeks.
vocab.exzh: 池塘裡停滯的水已經好幾週沒有流動了。

vocab.exzh: 月亮大約在一個月內經歷盈虧的變化。

vocab.exzh: 無論是過勞還是完全閒著，兩個極端對健康都不好。

vocab.exzh: 他情緒突然的變化讓每個人都感到很神祕。

quiz.q: According to the passage, what does the "opposition" relationship between yin and yang mean?
options: Yin and yang restrain each other so neither grows unchecked.
Yin and yang always oppose each other with no resolution.
Yin always defeats yang in the end.
Opposition means yin and yang cannot interact at all.

quiz.q: What comparison does the passage use for the "waxing and waning" relationship?
options: Water turning into steam.
Day gradually giving way to night and back again.
A shadow appearing without light.
Two magnets repelling each other.

quiz.q: According to the passage, what does the "transformation" relationship explain?
options: Why illnesses never change once they begin.
Why yin and yang can never affect each other.
Why a long, cold, quiet illness can suddenly flip into a hot, agitated state.
Why balance is always a fixed, unchanging point.

lessons.boundary_en: This lesson explains a theoretical framework, not a way to interpret your own symptoms. A sudden change in someone's condition should be evaluated by a licensed doctor, not matched against a reading passage.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這是理論框架的說明，不是拿來解讀自己症狀的工具；病情的突然變化，應該由合格醫師評估，而不是對照一篇文章。

lessons.title: Reading Your Own Yin-Yang Balance
lessons.blurb_en: Four everyday signs — temperature, energy, thirst, sleep — and why only the pattern over time matters.
lessons.blurb_zh: 體溫、精神、口渴、睡眠——四個日常觀察，重點是長期的模式，不是單一一天。
paras: Chinese medicine offers a simple, everyday way to notice which direction a person's yin and yang currently lean, long before anything becomes a medical problem. The signs are ordinary: temperature preference, energy through the day, thirst, and sleep. A person leaning toward yang excess or yin deficiency tends to run warm, prefer cold drinks, feel most energetic in the afternoon or evening, and sleep lightly or restlessly. A person leaning toward yang deficiency tends to run cold, especially in the hands and feet, prefer warm drinks, feel most sluggish in the morning, and sleep heavily but wake up unrefreshed.

None of these signs mean anything on their own. A single cold morning does not make someone "yang deficient," any more than one sleepless night makes someone "yin deficient." What matters is a pattern that holds steady over weeks, not an isolated day. This is also why Chinese medicine asks so many small, seemingly unrelated questions in a consultation — thirst, sleep, sweating, appetite, mood — because no single answer is diagnostic by itself. The pattern across all of them is.

The purpose of noticing these patterns in daily life is not to self-treat. It is to know your own baseline well enough to notice when something changes, and to describe that change clearly to a doctor. "I've been sleeping restlessly and craving cold drinks for the last month" is a far more useful sentence to bring into a clinic than "I don't feel like myself."
paras_zh: 中醫提供了一個簡單、日常就能觀察的方法，讓人能注意到自己的陰陽目前偏向哪個方向——遠在任何事情變成醫療問題之前。這些跡象都很平常：體溫偏好、一天中的精神狀態、口渴程度、睡眠品質。偏向陽亢或陰虛的人，通常容易覺得燥熱、偏好冰涼的飲料、在下午或傍晚精神最好、睡得淺或不安穩。偏向陽虛的人，通常容易怕冷，尤其是手腳，偏好溫熱的飲料，早上精神最差，睡得沉但醒來不解乏。
這些跡象單獨看都沒有意義。一個寒冷的早晨不能讓一個人變成「陽虛」，就像一個失眠的夜晚不能讓一個人變成「陰虛」。重要的是一個持續好幾週、穩定出現的模式，而不是單一一天的狀態。這也是為什麼中醫問診時會問許多看似不相關的小問題——口渴、睡眠、流汗、食慾、情緒——因為沒有任何單一答案本身能拿來診斷。所有答案合起來的模式才是關鍵。
在日常生活裡注意這些模式，目的不是自己治療。目的是清楚了解自己的基準狀態，好在有變化時能注意到，並且能把那個變化清楚地描述給醫師聽。「我這一個月睡得不安穩，很想喝冰的」比「我覺得不太對勁」對看診有用得多。
questions: According to the passage, what four everyday signs does Chinese medicine use to notice a person's yin-yang tendency?
Why does the passage say a single cold morning does not make someone "yang deficient"?
According to the last paragraph, what is the real purpose of noticing these patterns in daily life?
answers: Temperature preference, energy through the day, thirst, and sleep quality.
Because what matters is a pattern that holds steady over weeks, not a single, isolated day — one instance doesn't establish a lasting tendency.
Not to self-treat, but to know your own baseline well enough to notice a real change and describe it clearly to a doctor.

vocab.ex: He felt sluggish after staying up too late.
vocab.exzh: 他熬夜太晚之後覺得沒精神。

vocab.ex: She woke up unrefreshed despite sleeping nine hours.
vocab.exzh: 雖然睡了九小時，她醒來還是沒有恢復精神。

vocab.ex: One isolated mistake doesn't ruin a whole project.
vocab.exzh: 一個單一的錯誤不會毀掉整個專案。

vocab.ex: The doctor asked several questions during the consultation.
vocab.exzh: 醫師在問診過程中問了好幾個問題。

vocab.ex: Knowing your baseline heart rate helps you notice when something's off.
vocab.exzh: 了解你的基準心率，有助於察覺哪裡不對勁。

vocab.ex: In the summer, many people crave something cold to drink.
vocab.exzh: 在夏天，很多人都很想喝點冰涼的飲料。

vocab.ex: He has a tendency to work through lunch without noticing.
vocab.exzh: 他有不知不覺就邊工作邊吃午餐的傾向。

quiz.q: According to the passage, which of these is one of the four everyday signs used to notice yin-yang tendencies?
options: Handwriting style.
Thirst.
Shoe size.
Favorite color.

quiz.q: Why does the passage say a single sleepless night doesn't make someone "yin deficient"?
options: Because sleep has nothing to do with yin or yang.
Because only a pattern that holds steady over time is meaningful, not an isolated instance.
Because yin deficiency is not a real condition.
Because everyone is yin deficient at some point.

quiz.q: According to the passage, what is the real purpose of noticing your own daily patterns?
options: To diagnose and treat yourself without a doctor.
To win an argument with a doctor.
To know your baseline well enough to notice and describe real change to a doctor.
To avoid ever needing to see a doctor.

lessons.boundary_en: These are everyday observations, not a diagnostic checklist. A pattern worth noting is a reason to describe it clearly to a licensed doctor — not to self-treat based on this reading.
lessons.boundary_zh: 這些是日常觀察，不是診斷清單；值得注意的模式，是拿去清楚描述給合格醫師聽的理由，不是自行根據這篇文章治療的依據。

lessons.title: Explaining Yin-Yang to a Friend
lessons.blurb_en: A model answer for "Isn't yin-yang just a martial-arts symbol?" — built from everything covered in this unit.
lessons.blurb_zh: 當朋友問「陰陽不就是武術符號嗎？」，一段整合這個單元學過內容的示範回答。
paras: Suppose a friend asks, "Isn't yin-yang just a symbol from martial arts movies?" A good answer starts by separating the symbol from the idea. The black-and-white circle is a visual summary, not the concept itself, and the concept is worth explaining on its own terms: "Yin and yang describe two complementary functions in the body — substance and activity, cooling and warming, rest and movement. Neither one is 'good' or 'bad.' They're more like inhaling and exhaling: both necessary, neither one superior."

Next, it helps to explain why the idea matters practically, not just philosophically: "When a doctor of Chinese medicine says someone's yang is weak, they mean the warming and moving side of the body's functions isn't strong enough — the person feels cold, moves slowly, prefers warmth. It's a description of function, the same way saying someone has 'low energy' describes a pattern without claiming to have found a single broken part." This keeps the explanation grounded in something concrete rather than mystical.

Finally, it's worth naming what yin-yang is not: "It's not a fixed personality type, and it's not a horoscope. It's not something a person 'is' once and for all — it shifts throughout the day, the seasons, and a person's life, and a doctor's job is to notice which direction it's currently leaning, not to hand out a permanent label." Ending on this note keeps a friend from walking away thinking yin-yang works like a zodiac sign.
paras_zh: 假設一位朋友問：「陰陽不就是武術電影裡的一個符號嗎？」一個好的回答要先把符號跟概念分開。黑白相間的圓形圖案是一種視覺上的濃縮，不是概念本身，概念值得用它自己的方式來解釋：「陰陽描述的是身體裡兩種互補的功能——物質與活動、寒涼與溫熱、休息與活動。沒有哪一個是『好』或『壞』的。它們比較像吸氣跟呼氣：兩者都是必要的，沒有誰比較優越。」
接著，解釋這個概念為什麼在實際上有意義，而不只是哲學上有意義會有幫助：「當中醫師說一個人的陽虛，意思是身體功能裡溫煦與推動的那一側不夠強——這個人會怕冷、動作變慢、偏好溫暖。這是一種功能上的描述，就像說一個人『沒什麼精神』是在描述一種模式，而不是聲稱找到了某個壞掉的零件。」這讓解釋保持在具體的層面，而不是神祕的層面。
最後，值得講清楚陰陽不是什麼：「它不是一種固定的人格類型，也不是星座。它不是一個人一次性、永久地『就是』什麼——它會隨著一天、季節、一個人的人生階段而改變，醫師的工作是注意它目前偏向哪個方向，而不是發一個永久的標籤。」用這句話收尾，能避免朋友離開時覺得陰陽的運作方式就像星座一樣。
questions: According to the passage, why does a good explanation of yin-yang start by separating the symbol from the idea?
What everyday comparison does the passage use to explain why neither yin nor yang is "better" than the other?
According to the last paragraph, what is yin-yang NOT, and why does the passage say ending on that note matters?
answers: Because the black-and-white circle is only a visual summary, not the concept itself, so starting with it risks the listener mistaking a symbol for an explanation.
It compares yin and yang to inhaling and exhaling — both are necessary, and neither one is superior to the other.

Yin-yang is not a fixed personality type or a horoscope — it shifts over time. Ending on this note matters because it prevents a friend from mistakenly thinking yin-yang assigns a permanent label, like a zodiac sign.

vocab.ex: Neither team felt superior after the tied match.
vocab.exzh: 平手之後，兩隊都不覺得自己比較優越。

vocab.ex: Her explanation stayed grounded in real examples, not abstract theory.
vocab.exzh: 她的解釋一直立足於真實的例子，而不是抽象的理論。

vocab.ex: He was drawn to the mystical side of ancient philosophy.
vocab.exzh: 他被古代哲學神祕的一面吸引。

vocab.ex: A tattoo is meant to be permanent.
vocab.exzh: 刺青本來就是要永久的。

vocab.ex: She reads her horoscope every morning, just for fun.
vocab.exzh: 她每天早上都看星座運勢，純粹好玩。

vocab.ex: His opinion tends to lean toward caution rather than risk.
vocab.exzh: 他的意見傾向謹慎，而不是冒險。

quiz.q: According to the passage, why should a good explanation of yin-yang separate the symbol from the idea?
options: Because the symbol is more important than the idea.
Because the black-and-white circle is only a visual summary, not the concept itself.
Because the symbol is banned in some countries.
Because there is no real concept behind the symbol.

quiz.q: What comparison does the passage use to explain why neither yin nor yang is "better" than the other?
options: Two rival sports teams.
Inhaling and exhaling.
Night and day in a horoscope.
Hot and cold water mixed together.

quiz.q: According to the passage, what is yin-yang NOT, according to the explanation given to the friend?
options: A description of bodily function.
A fixed personality type or horoscope.
A concept used in Chinese medicine.
Something that can shift over time.

lessons.boundary_en: Explaining yin-yang to a friend is a cultural and language exercise, not medical advice. Real health questions always belong with a licensed doctor, not a casual conversation.
lessons.boundary_zh: 跟朋友解釋陰陽是文化與語言的練習，不是醫療建議；真正的健康問題永遠該交給合格醫師，不是閒聊。
